sections.h2: Where does a Wood County deed get filed?
sections.html:
Deeds for Wood County land are filed at the Recorder's office in Bowling Green, in the County Office Building at One Courthouse Square (second floor). Phone 419-354-9140. The front counter opens at 8:30 and closes at 4:30 on weekdays, and the office is shut on Saturday and Sunday.

The county seat moved from Perrysburg to Bowling Green in 1870, and the present courthouse was begun in 1893. Wood County spans 620 square miles along the Maumee River and belongs to the Toledo metro area. The 2020 census counted 132,248 residents and 56,863 housing units, with 65.9 percent of occupied units owner held. Bowling Green State University is the largest employer on the county's 2019 list, so the Recorder sees a steady stream of both student-area rentals and suburban Perrysburg and Rossford sales.

Three county offices touch every sale. The Recorder keeps the permanent record. The Auditor moves taxable ownership on the tax rolls. The Treasurer, reachable at 419-354-9130, collects what is owed on the parcel.

sections.h2: What must a Wood County deed contain to be accepted?
sections.html:
The grantor signs, and a notary or another authorized officer certifies the signature (Revised Code 5301.01). The deed then goes to the Recorder for the county where the land sits, because Revised Code 5301.25 treats an unrecorded deed as fraudulent against a later good faith buyer.

The Recorder's website carries document standards and a note on marginal references. A marginal reference points back to an earlier paper by instrument number, or by book and page. A release should name the mortgage it ends. A deed that cites the prior deed pays no separate index charge, while a cited land contract or ended life estate is indexed and priced as a reference. Before mailing a deed, run down this list:

  • The signature and notary block are complete.
  • The legal description copies the last recorded deed, or a newer survey.
  • The Auditor's endorsement is on the face of the deed.
  • The fee covers every page, caption page included.

sections.h2: What does it cost to file a deed in Wood County?
sections.html:
Revised Code 317.32 builds each charge from two halves: a recording fee and an equal housing trust fund fee. Seventeen dollars of each covers a first two pages, and four dollars of each covers every extra page. The county can tack on a preservation surcharge capped at five dollars. The Wood County Recorder's site has a fee estimator that totals your document.

Pages are measured at eight and a half by fourteen inches and a partial page counts as a full one, so a deed with a long exhibit costs more. The table shows the figures a house seller is most likely to meet.

Statutory recording charges, with the Wood County copy rate
ChargePrinted amount
Pages one and two$17 base plus $17 housing trust fund
Every further page$4 base plus $4 housing trust fund
Preservation surchargeUp to $5
Reference entered by a separate instrument$2 base plus $2 housing trust fund for each
Copy of a recorded page, Wood County$2.00 per page

Sources: Ohio Revised Code 317.32 and the Wood County Recorder contact page.

sections.h2: Why does the Auditor see a Wood County deed before the Recorder does?
sections.html:
The Auditor, at 419-354-9150, takes the buyer's statement of value and stamps the conveyance fee on the deed. Only then does it go to the Recorder. The fee under Revised Code 319.54 is the larger of one dollar or ten cents per hundred dollars of value, and the grantor pays it.

A county can also pass its own transfer tax, up to thirty cents per hundred dollars (Revised Code 322.02), collected by the Auditor before recording. Ask the Auditor whether Wood County has one before you build a net sheet.

sections.h2: How do I search Wood County records or order a copy?
sections.html:
The Recorder's site offers three search paths. Adaptable Visual Access shows the index from 1980 forward and trails the real filing date by roughly a day. A Laredo Anywhere account shows document images, but the office designed it for high volume professional users and asks for an account request form. AmeriScan's Documents-On-Demand shows the old physical book indexes.

State law, in Revised Code 317.13, set June 30, 2026 as the date by which each recorder had to publish electronic indexes and images for everything recorded since January 1, 1980, and had to accept electronic recording of conveyances. A recorder may not charge for the login itself.

Copies cost $2.00 per page. The office wants an instrument number or a book and page with every request, and staff will not open a document to look for a legal description. A typical order runs like this:

  • Search the index by name and write down the instrument number.
  • Decide whether you want the whole document or only certain pages. The first or last page needs no extra identification.
  • Send the number and page choice by email or phone.

sections.h2: Which Wood County cities and school districts should a seller name?
sections.html:
Wood County has five cities: Bowling Green, Northwood, Perrysburg and Rossford, plus a small slice of Fostoria. Fifteen school districts reach into the county, among them Bowling Green City, Perrysburg Exempted Village, Rossford Exempted Village, Anthony Wayne Local, Eastwood Local, Elmwood Local, Lake Local, Otsego Local and Patrick Henry Local. A buyer will ask which district a house belongs to, so check the tax bill rather than guessing from the mailing address.

Fort Meigs, built during the War of 1812, gave the county its name through the engineer Captain Eleazer D. Wood. Perrysburg held the first county seat from the 1820 founding. Today the Wood County Airport sits northeast of downtown Bowling Green, and the Maumee River forms the diagonal northwest edge of the county.

If a paid mortgage never got a recorded release, ask the lender for one and record it with a marginal reference to the original. Then call the Treasurer to learn whether any tax remains on the parcel.

faqs.q: How much is the recording fee for a Wood County deed?
faqs.a: The statute prices the first two pages at $17 plus a $17 housing trust fund fee, and each later page at $4 plus $4, with an optional preservation surcharge up to $5. The fee estimator on the Wood County Recorder's site totals your own document.

faqs.q: Does Wood County charge a transfer tax on a sale?
faqs.a: The conveyance fee through the Auditor applies to most sales and the seller pays it. A county transfer tax applies only if the commissioners adopted one, so call the Auditor at 419-354-9150.

faqs.q: Can I get a copy of my deed without driving to Bowling Green?
faqs.a: Yes. Find the instrument number in the online index and send it by phone or email. Copies are $2.00 per page.

faqs.q: How far back do the online Wood County records go?
faqs.a: The index starts in 1980 and runs about a day behind. Older records are in book indexes served through AmeriScan.

faqs.q: Who is hurt if a signed deed is never recorded?
faqs.a: The buyer. A later good faith purchaser can beat an unrecorded deed, so the buyer should record right after closing.
